question.text: Himalaya Growth Fund (Cat II AIF) subscribes to equity shares of Shivpuri Tech Pvt Ltd at INR 150 per share, while FMV (by merchant banker) is INR 100 per share — i.e., share issued at a PREMIUM above FMV. 10 lakh shares are subscribed. The issuance is on or after 1 April 2024 (AY 2025-26). What is the tax impact under the erstwhile Section 56(2)(viib) ('angel tax') on the Indian investee company?

answer.text: No angel tax — Section 56(2)(viib) has been made inapplicable from AY 2025-26 (Finance (No.2) Act 2024); the INR 50 x 10 lakh = INR 5 crore premium over FMV is NOT taxed as deemed income in the investee company
Investee pays tax at 30% on INR 5 crore as income from other sources
Fund pays the angel tax on behalf of the investee
Investor LPs pay angel tax on their respective pro-rata share

explanation.text: The Logic: Workbook Para 16.1.4: Section 56(2)(viib) taxed the INVESTEE company on any premium over FMV received on issue of shares. Finance (No.2) Act 2024 made this section INAPPLICABLE from AY 2025-26 onwards. So for issuances on or after 1 April 2024, no angel tax. The historic exemption for consideration received from Cat I/II AIFs has thus been rendered moot — the provision itself is gone. The Trap: Option B is the pre-AY-2025-26 charging logic — now abolished. Option C confuses who bears the tax (was the investee, not the fund). Option D invents an LP-level charge. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A and XV touch on angel tax; XIX-C requires granular understanding of pre/post cutover for post-FA 2024 fundraises. Manager's Pro-Tip: If your Cat II fund invests in early-stage companies, time any 'premium' rounds post 1 April 2024 to avoid 56(2)(viib). Also get a merchant-banker FMV certificate contemporaneously with the subscription — the FMV anchor is still your first line of defence against any other deeming provision.
